[All benchmarks](../benchmarks.qmd)

An account review team has a limited investigation budget. It needs an estimate
of expected loss over the next month, alongside the individual transactions
that may attract disputes. This benchmark asks whether purchase baskets and a
separate withdrawal history would help prioritize that review.

::: {.callout-note title="Fictional benchmark"}
All data, schemas, and results on this page are fictional placeholders.
No benchmark has been run.
:::

## Example

One row is an account snapshot at a common review cutoff of May 28, 2026 at
14:30. Transactions and withdrawals contain only information known then.
Every transaction's `disputed` label describes a new dispute reported during
the following 30 days; `loss_next_30_days` is the account's realized loss over
that same window, in the application's common currency.

```yaml
account_id: account-42
account_age_days: 420
trxns:
  - booked_at: "2026-05-21T10:00:00"
    amount: 32.00
    merchant: Station Cafe
    channel: card
    line_items:
      - sku: lunch
        quantity: 2
    disputed: false
  - booked_at: "2026-05-27T18:15:00"
    amount: 56.20
    merchant: North Market
    channel: card
    line_items:
      - sku: groceries
        quantity: 1
      - sku: household-supplies
        quantity: 2
    disputed: true
  - booked_at: "2026-05-28T14:30:00"
    amount: 84.50
    merchant: North Market
    channel: card
    line_items:
      - sku: groceries
        quantity: 1
    disputed: false
recent_cash_withdrawals:
  - booked_at: "2026-05-26T16:00:00"
    amount: 100.00
    atm_region: home_region
loss_next_30_days: 18.50
```

The labels above belong to a settled training observation. At scoring time,
omit every `disputed` value and `loss_next_30_days`. `account_id` is an
application identifier carried alongside the modeled fields.

## Schema

Line items describe the contents of each purchase. Withdrawals form an
independent history, since an ATM event has neither a merchant nor a purchase
basket. Both histories contribute to the account loss estimate, while each
transaction also receives its own dispute prediction.

```{typst}
//| label: fig-benchmark-account-loss
//| fig-cap: "Fictional account-loss schema: purchase baskets and withdrawals add context to transaction and account targets."
//| fig-alt: "An account contains account_age_days, repeated trxns, repeated recent_cash_withdrawals, and the Number target loss_next_30_days. Each transaction contains booked_at DateParts, amount Number, merchant Category, channel Enum, repeated line_items with sku Category and quantity Number, and the Boolean target disputed. Each withdrawal contains booked_at DateParts, amount Number, and atm_region Category. Both targets are always hidden from input."
#tree(node("account", kind: "root", children: (
  node("account_age_days", width: 150pt, type: "Number"),
  node("trxns", kind: "branch", repeated: true, children: (
    node("booked_at", type: "DateParts"),
    node("amount", type: "Number"),
    node("merchant", type: "Category"),
    node("channel", type: "Enum"),
    node("line_items", kind: "branch", repeated: true, children: (
      node("sku", type: "Category"),
      node("quantity", type: "Number"),
    )),
    node("disputed", kind: "target", type: "Boolean", body: [Always hidden.]),
  )),
  node("recent_cash_withdrawals", width: 185pt, kind: "branch", repeated: true, children: (
    node("booked_at", type: "DateParts"),
    node("amount", type: "Number"),
    node("atm_region", type: "Category"),

  node("loss_next_30_days", width: 165pt, kind: "target", type: "Number", body: [Always hidden.]),
```

<details>
<summary>Complete model schema</summary>

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.md(
    account_age_days=rf.Number,
    trxns=rf.Branch(
        length=64,
        overflow="tail",
        booked_at=rf.DateParts(
            dateparts=["day_of_month", "day_of_week", "hour_of_day"],
        ),
        amount=rf.Number,
        merchant=rf.Category,
        channel=rf.Enum(values=("card", "direct_debit", "bank_transfer")),
        line_items=rf.Branch(
            length=16,
            overflow="head",
            sku=rf.Category,
            quantity=rf.Number,
        ),
        disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
    ),
    recent_cash_withdrawals=rf.Branch(
        length=16,
        overflow="tail",
        booked_at=rf.DateParts(
            dateparts=["day_of_month", "day_of_week", "hour_of_day"],
        ),
        amount=rf.Number,
        atm_region=rf.Category,
    ),
    loss_next_30_days=rf.Number(mask=True),
)
```

Keep each history oldest to newest. The caps retain the last 64 transactions
and last 16 withdrawals; each transaction retains its first 16 supplied line
items. The two histories have independent coordinates. Booking-time
`DateParts` provide calendar features, not exact elapsed durations.

</details>

## Comparison

Keep the account profile, transaction inputs, both target definitions, and
review windows fixed. Train three separate models with the same `md` preset
and training budget. First use transactions without line items or withdrawals;
then add purchase baskets; finally add the withdrawal history. This isolates
which added context would account for any change.

The primary measure is mean absolute error in account loss, including accounts
with zero loss. Also report the share of disputed transactions captured in
the highest-scored 10% of transactions, so a better account estimate cannot
silently hide worse transaction review performance.

## Result

| Available context | Account loss MAE ↓ | Disputes captured in top 10% ↑ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Profile and transactions | 4.80 | 41% |
| Add purchase line items | 4.35 | 44% |
| Add separate withdrawals | 4.10 | 45% |

: Fictional placeholder results. MAE is in the application's common currency units. {#tbl-benchmark-account-loss-results}

The example tracks how added context affects the account estimate and the
transaction ranking separately. A measured comparison would report uncertainty
for both outcomes.

<details>
<summary>Proposed data and evaluation protocol</summary>

**Fictional data contract.** An application would supply nested Parquet
observations using the schema above:

| Split | Illustrative path | Proposed account snapshots |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Train | `benchmarks/account-loss/train.parquet` | 400,000 |
| Validation | `benchmarks/account-loss/validation.parquet` | 50,000 |
| Test | `benchmarks/account-loss/test.parquet` | 50,000 |

Use disjoint account groups across splits and later review cutoffs for validation and test.
Leave at least the 30-day outcome window between the last training cutoff and
the first validation cutoff, and again before test. Only include snapshots
whose entire outcome window has settled. Fit category and numeric preparation
on training observations and reuse it unchanged.

**Workload.** The proposed source contains 1–64 retained transactions per
account, 1–16 line items per purchase, and 0–16 withdrawals. Record the actual
length distributions, null rates, category counts, and label prevalence when
real data replace these placeholders. Use the same source observations and
retained transactions for every comparison; remove only the context being
tested. Both targets remain supervised in every configuration.

**Training plan.** Use the same optimizer settings, batch size of 128 account
observations, maximum 30 epochs, and three matched seeds for each schema.
Choose checkpoints using validation account-loss MAE under a rule fixed before
test. Report per-seed test results and their spread, plus account-level
bootstrap intervals.

**Decision rule.** Rank transactions globally at a fixed 10% review budget and
calculate captured disputes on all retained test transactions. Account MAE
uses one loss estimate per snapshot in the same common currency. Report
calibration and error for loss-bearing accounts separately before using either
output to allocate review capacity.

</details>
